edits.text: Share Purchase Agreement — Discussion Draft; Subject to Contract
edits.name: Draft status

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD [●] (the “Purchase Price”). No purchase-price proposal is made by this placeholder. Subject to agreement on payment mechanics, at Closing the Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Seller’s designated account. The Seller shall provide payment instructions at least three Business Days before Closing, and the Buyer shall verify those instructions through an independently established contact before payment. No adjustment, escrow, holdback, deferred payment, or other payment arrangement applies unless expressly set out in the executed Agreement. “Business Day” means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or a public holiday in New York, New York.
edits.name: Price and payment

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur by electronic exchange of documents and funds on the fifth Business Day after satisfaction or written waiver of the conditions below, other than conditions to be satisfied at Closing, or on another date agreed in writing. Each party’s obligation to close is conditioned on the absence of any law or order prohibiting the transaction and receipt of all legally required regulatory approvals. The Buyer’s obligation is also conditioned on: (a) the Seller’s representations being true in all material respects at Closing, except representations qualified by materiality, which must be true as written, and representations made as of a specified date, which are tested as of that date; (b) the Seller having performed its pre-Closing obligations in all material respects; (c) receipt of the third-party consents expressly identified in the agreed closing schedule; and (d) delivery of duly executed instruments transferring good title to the Shares free of liens, applicable share certificates or equivalent ownership records, evidence of the Seller’s authority, an updated ownership register where legally required, and a certificate confirming satisfaction of conditions (a) and (b). The Seller’s obligation is conditioned on the Buyer having performed its pre-Closing obligations in all material respects and delivering the Purchase Price, evidence of authority, and a certificate confirming such performance. Conditions may be waived only in writing by the party benefited, and no legally mandatory condition may be waived. Deliveries and payment are concurrent, and Closing does not occur until all have been completed or validly waived. If Closing has not occurred within sixty days after execution, either party may terminate by written notice, unless its material breach caused the failure to close; termination does not extinguish accrued claims. Before execution, the parties shall complete a closing schedule identifying each required approval and consent, the relevant authority or counterparty, and the required evidence of receipt.
edits.name: Closing conditions and deliverables

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents at execution and at Closing that: (a) it has capacity and authority to execute and perform this Agreement; (b) it owns the Shares, has authority to transfer them, and will transfer good title free of liens; (c) the Company is duly organized and validly existing, and its capitalization and all outstanding rights to acquire its securities are accurately stated in the disclosure schedules; (d) execution and performance do not violate its organizational documents, applicable law, or any material contract, except for consents expressly listed in the disclosure schedules; (e) the financial statements identified and attached in the disclosure schedules were prepared consistently with the accounting framework expressly identified there and fairly present, in all material respects, the Company’s financial position and results for the stated periods, subject, for unaudited statements only, to disclosed normal year-end adjustments and absence of notes; (f) the Company has no liabilities except those reflected or reserved in those statements, expressly disclosed in the disclosure schedules, or incurred in the ordinary course since the latest balance-sheet date and not arising from a breach of law or contract; and (g) the disclosure schedules accurately identify material contracts, pending litigation, and written claims of material legal noncompliance, and all material tax returns required to be filed have been filed and material taxes due have been paid, except as expressly disclosed. The Buyer represents that it is duly organized and validly existing, has authority to execute and perform this Agreement, and will have sufficient immediately available funds at Closing. Disclosures qualify a representation only where specifically cross-referenced or where their relevance is reasonably apparent from the disclosure’s text; access to a data room alone is not disclosure. Neither party makes any representation beyond those expressly stated in this Agreement, and no forecast or projection is warranted. This limitation does not exclude liability for fraud. Before execution, the parties shall agree and attach the financial statements, accounting framework, capitalization schedule, and complete disclosure schedules.
edits.name: Representations and disclosures

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. After Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer and the Company against actual losses, liabilities, damages, and reasonable external defense costs resulting from a breach of the Seller’s representations or covenants, Company taxes attributable to periods ending on or before Closing, and Company liabilities existing at Closing other than liabilities reflected or reserved in the agreed financial statements, expressly disclosed in the disclosure schedules, or incurred in the ordinary course since the latest balance-sheet date without breach of law or contract. The Buyer shall indemnify the Seller against corresponding losses resulting from a breach of the Buyer’s representations or covenants. General representations survive for eighteen months after Closing; authority, title, and capitalization representations survive for six years; tax claims survive until sixty days after expiration of the applicable assessment period; and covenants survive according to their terms. A claim notified with reasonable factual detail and an estimated amount, if reasonably ascertainable, before expiry survives until resolved. General representation claims are recoverable only to the extent their aggregate exceeds one percent of the Purchase Price, and aggregate liability for those claims is capped at twenty percent of the Purchase Price. Authority, title, capitalization, tax, undisclosed-liability, and covenant claims are outside that deductible and cap, but aggregate liability under this Section shall not exceed the Purchase Price. No contractual deductible, cap, or survival restriction applies to a party’s own fraud. The claimant shall give reasonably prompt written notice; delay reduces recovery only to the extent of actual prejudice. For a third-party claim, the indemnifying party may assume the defense within twenty Business Days using reasonably acceptable counsel if it acknowledges coverage in writing and the claim seeks solely monetary relief without a material conflict of interest. Otherwise, the claimant controls the defense. The other party may participate at its own expense, except that reasonable separate-counsel costs are recoverable where a material conflict requires separate representation. Neither party may settle a covered claim without the other’s written consent, not unreasonably withheld; no settlement may impose an admission, nonmonetary obligation, or liability on the other party without its express consent and an unconditional release. For direct claims, the recipient shall respond within thirty days; silence is not acceptance, and unresolved claims may be pursued in a court of competent jurisdiction. Each claimant shall take reasonable steps to mitigate loss. Recovery excludes punitive damages and speculative or duplicative loss, except amounts payable to a third party, and is reduced by insurance proceeds and tax benefits actually realized from the same loss, net of reasonable recovery costs. No loss may be recovered twice or to the extent already reflected in a purchase-price adjustment. Indemnification is the exclusive post-Closing monetary remedy for matters covered by this Section, except fraud; claims for payment of the Purchase Price and equitable relief remain available.
edits.name: Indemnity scope and procedures
